plant_name: Luoyuan Times New Energy Battery Industrial Base (Luoyuan)
research_notes: CATL's Luoyuan battery base in Songshan A area, Fuzhou Taishang Investment Zone, Luoyuan County, Fuzhou, Fujian province (adjacent to CATL's Ningde HQ, ~30 min away). Investment contract signed 2 Jan 2025; project company "Luoyuan Times New Energy Technology Co., Ltd." (罗源时代新能源科技有限公司, wholly-owned CATL subsidiary, registered 7 Mar 2025, registered capital RMB 2bn, legal rep Chen Weifeng). Phase I construction officially began 24 April 2025. Total investment RMB 6.5bn; land ~900 mu (~60 ha); planned annual capacity ~40 GWh of new-energy batteries. Confirmed by multiple sources (EnergyTrend, metal.com/SMM, Fuzhou/Fujian government releases, OFweek). Status: under construction. Chemistry, cell format, end market (EV/ESS) and exact production start year not specified in available sources, so left null. This is a CATL battery-cell manufacturing base (not pack-only), hence is_cell_manufacturer=true. No JV — single wholly-owned CATL operator. Exact site coordinates not sourced (Luoyuan County approx 26.49N, 119.55E) so lat/long left null to avoid a guessed value. Note: distinct from CATL's Luoyang (Henan) plant and other Fujian bases.

plant_name: CATL Dongying Zero-Carbon Industrial Park (lithium battery manufacturing base)
research_notes: Distinct from CATL's Jining base (60 GWh Phase 1, operational May 2025) — some search results conflate the two Shandong sites; this is the separate Dongying project. Located in Kenli District, Dongying, Shandong. Strategic cooperation agreement signed 15 Mar 2025; project broke ground 26 Jul 2025 as the "Dongying Times Zero-Carbon Industrial Park", billed as China's first industrial park run entirely on direct-connect renewable (off public grid, local wind + solar). Phase 1 = 40 GWh lithium-battery green intelligent manufacturing base, expected completion/operation in 2026 (hence status under_construction as of July 2025 sources). Investment >10bn yuan (~US$1.39bn) for Phase 1; ~2,400 jobs; ~26bn yuan annual output projected. Phase 2 announced ("at an appropriate time") but no capacity figure disclosed, so nameplate reflects Phase 1 only. Specific chemistry (LFP vs NMC) and end market (EV vs ESS) not disclosed — left null. A separate, smaller "Dongying Era" 2 GWh ESS battery PACK project (~500m yuan) exists nearby but is pack assembly, not this cell base. Precise plant coordinates not published; Kenli District only — coordinates left null rather than guessed. Corroborated by China Daily (2025-07-30), Gasgoo, SMM/Metal.com, and CATL's own release (catl.com/en/news/6397.html, returned 403 to fetch but cited across trackers).

plant_name: Sunwoda Yichang power battery production base
research_notes: Power battery (EV) cell manufacturing base in Yichang, Hubei province, China. Operated by Hubei Dongyu Xinsheng New Energy Co., Ltd., a JV between Sunwoda Energy/Sunwoda Power (EVB) and Dongfeng Motor Group (Dongfeng Hongtai). Total investment RMB 12bn (~$1.6-1.7bn). Planned 30 GWh/yr in two phases: Phase 1 = 20 GWh, Phase 2 = 10 GWh. Construction started 30 Oct 2022; first battery cells officially delivered Oct 2023 (313 days from trial production), so Phase 1 is operational. nameplate_capacity_gwh=30 is the full/eventual two-phase nameplate; capacity_by_year_json reflects Phase 1 (20 GWh from 2023) ramping toward 30 GWh — exact Phase 2 completion year not confirmed, 2025 assumed. Chemistry and cell format not confirmed by sources (Sunwoda power cells are typically NMC and LFP, but not verified for this site) — left null. Coordinates not sourced — left null. Cross-checked against CnEVPost, electrive, EnergyTrend/EQ Mag and Chinese sources (Hubei govt, Gasgoo) all citing 30 GWh two-phase base and the Dongfeng JV.

plant_name: Sunwoda Deyang (Shifang) power and energy storage battery base
research_notes: The "Deyang plant" is Sunwoda's base in Shifang (什邡), a county-level city under Deyang prefecture, Sichuan. Signed with Shifang govt in 2022 (project kick-off 25 May 2022; main structure completed 30 Sep 2022, "Deyang speed"). Total investment ~RMB 10bn, 700+ mu (mu = ~0.067 ha) site. A 25 GWh power+storage battery line was put into operation in 2023 (operational). Positioned as the group's strategic ENERGY STORAGE production base; makes 314Ah LFP prismatic storage cells for grid-level and commercial ESS. Phase-1 design 25 GWh across three lines; ~17 GWh reported built as of 2025, with a third line (adding ~7.4 GWh) under construction/ramping in 2025 and a new 684Ah storage cell targeted for mass production early 2026. H1 2025 deliveries/shipments reportedly doubled y/y, making it the group's fastest-growing storage engine. Wholly owned by Sunwoda (not a JV). Coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Capacity_by_year ramp not cleanly sourced (25 GWh design vs ~17 GWh built), left null rather than guessed. Nameplate figure sometimes described alongside a broader Sichuan plan (earlier 2022 reports cite a 20 GWh Shifang base); 25 GWh is the figure tied to the operational Deyang/Shifang base. Corroborated by jiemian.com, sohu, electrive.com and ess-news.com.

plant_name: Sunwoda Maoming (Dianbai) automotive electronics base
research_notes: This site is NOT a battery cell plant. The Sunwoda base in Dianbai district, Maoming (Guangdong) is an automotive-electronics production base manufacturing battery management systems (BMS), body control modules (BCM) and vehicle control units (VCU) for EVs — no cell/electrode manufacturing. Agreement with Dianbai district signed Dec 2022 (~RMB 4bn planned investment, ~100 mu, two phases); base officially opened 27 Dec 2023 with first lines in production. Phase-1 plan: 24 SMT + 48 DIP lines, ~3m sets/year at full ramp (units are sets, not GWh — not applicable to cell capacity). Sunwoda's actual cell gigafactories are elsewhere (Zhuhai ~30 GWh, Yiwu ~50 GWh, Nanchang/Quzhou, Beijing Shunyi ~41 GWh). No sourced coordinates found. Confidence reflects clear, multiply-corroborated evidence that this is not a cell site; exact site geodata unconfirmed. Corroborating Chinese-language sources: gd.people.com.cn, bjx.com.cn (20231227/1352609), sunwoda.com/article/996.

plant_name: Sunwoda Nanjing power battery base (Lishui)
research_notes: Sunwoda's first power-battery production base in East China, located in the Lishui Economic Development Zone, Lishui District, Nanjing, Jiangsu. Produces lithium-ion battery CELLS (电芯) plus modules and packs — confirmed cell manufacturer. Positioned as a HEV/power-battery and fast-charging cell base, so end_market treated as EV (power). Total investment reported ~CNY 12bn (some sources ~CNY 13.5bn), planned total nameplate 30 GWh/yr built in three phases: phase 1 ~8 GWh, phase 2 +10 GWh, phase 3 +12 GWh. nameplate_capacity_gwh=30 is the eventual full planned nameplate (no single reference year confirmed, so capacity_ref_year left null). Site is operational: local reports describe "signed, built and into production in the same year", and by Aug 2023 phase 1 was ramping (~300 cells/minute off the line) with phase 2 under construction. start_year set to 2022 based on 2022 output of ~CNY 8bn (+344% YoY) indicating phase-1 production had begun; not precisely confirmed. Chemistry and cell format not confirmed per-plant (Sunwoda power cells are typically NMC/LFP) so left null. Coordinates not sourced precisely, left null rather than guessed. Phase-by-year ramp not firmly dated, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Sources: sina finance (2023-08-30) on the Lishui base; corroborated by 21jingji (Sep 2022) and Chinese trade press (OFweek). Distinct from Sunwoda's JV cell base with Dongfeng in Yichang and the Beijing Shunyi (41.32 GWh) project — this is the standalone Nanjing/Lishui site, not a JV.

plant_name: Sunwoda Huizhou plant (Huizhou Liwei New Energy)
operator: Huizhou Liwei New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (Sunwoda)
research_notes:
Identity: "Sunwoda Huizhou plant" maps to Huizhou Liwei New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (惠州锂威新能源科技有限公司), established September 2016 in Sunwoda Industrial Park, Yuanzhou town, Boluo County, Huizhou, Guangdong. It is a wholly-owned cell-making subsidiary under Dongguan Liwei Energy, itself wholly owned by Sunwoda Electronic. Liwei (锂威 / LIWINON) is Sunwoda's dedicated consumer (3C) cell brand.

Cell manufacturer: YES. The site manufactures lithium-ion polymer (pouch) CELLS for smartphones, tablets, laptops and wearables (customers include Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi). Not pack-only.

Capacity: company/park sources state ~600,000 consumer cells/day, total investment ~RMB 3bn, ~180,000 m² building area, fully automated lines. This is a per-unit (cells/day) figure, not a GWh/year figure; consumer cells are small so a GWh number cannot be derived reliably from public data — left null rather than guessed. An unverified low-quality summary suggested a Huizhou base of ~4 GWh, not used.

Chemistry: sourced as "lithium-ion polymer" consumer cells; high-energy consumer polymer cells are typically LCO (some NMC-blend). Recorded honestly as inferred.

Status: operational (in production since ~2016-2017, supplying major OEMs). announced_year=2016 (subsidiary set up / announced Oct 2016 per cbea.com). start_year left null (exact first-production year not confirmed).

Ambiguity: some low-quality summaries also refer to a Sunwoda "Huizhou power-battery base"; the well-documented Sunwoda cell facility in Huizhou is the Liwei consumer-cell plant, which is what this record describes. Coordinates left null (only town-level location known: Yuanzhou, Boluo County ~23.1N,114.0E — not recorded to avoid a guessed precise value).

Secondary source: cbea.com (电池中国网) announcement of establishment of Huizhou Liwei subsidiary, Oct 2016 — http://www.cbea.com/lxwd/201610/86460.html

plant_name: Sunwoda Quzhou plant
research_notes: Sunwoda's Quzhou (Zhejiang) base manufactures the company's 684 Ah large-format LFP energy storage cells (stacked prismatic, >440 Wh/L, grid-scale ESS). It is one of two sites (with Nanchang, Jiangxi) designated for this cell, with a COMBINED 10 GWh/year initial nameplate; the site-level split is not disclosed, so nameplate_capacity_gwh left null rather than guessed. Status operational: the 684 Ah cell entered mass production in September 2025, with the one-millionth unit delivered by end December 2025 (ess-news, 2025-12-29). announced_year 2024 inferred from the project's inclusion in Zhejiang's 14th Five-Year New Energy plan / 2024 "Thousand Projects" initiative (lower confidence). Coordinates not found in reputable sources. Chemistry LFP confirmed by multiple sources; Sunwoda ESS cells reported at full production/full sales. Sources: pv magazine / ess-news 2025-08-27; ess-news 2025-12-29 (one-millionth cell); Sunwoda 2025 interim report.

plant_name: Chaowei Anqing Chaoren Sodium-Ion Battery Plant (Phase I)
operator: Anqing Chaoren Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
research_notes: Site is in Anqing, Anhui province, China, operated by Anqing Chaoren Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (established July 2022), a subsidiary of Chaowei Power Group (Chilwee). Phase I (2 GWh/yr) was formally put into production on 13 June 2026, hence status = operational; total planned nameplate across all phases is 6.5 GWh/yr on a ~324.5 mu (~21.6 ha) site, total investment RMB 3.5bn (~US$517m). nameplate_capacity_gwh = 6.5 is the eventual full nameplate; capacity_by_year_json records the confirmed 2 GWh operational in 2026. capacity_ref_year left null because sources give no target year for the full 6.5 GWh. Chemistry is sodium-ion, using Chaowei's NFPP (sodium ferric pyrophosphate/Prussian-blue-family) cathode; the plant is described as producing low-temperature traction cells for entry-level EVs (Chaowei supplies Chery), so end_market set to EV, though Chaowei sodium cells are also marketed for ESS. cell_format not confirmed by sources (null). No verified site coordinates found, so latitude/longitude left null rather than guessed. Cross-checked across carnewschina (16 Jun 2026), China Battery Industry Association / cbea.com, and China.com trade press; core facts (2 GWh phase I, 6.5 GWh total, RMB 3.5bn, 13 Jun 2026 start) are consistent across sources. Confidence 0.8: multiple reputable trade sources agree, but no single primary company IR document accessed and some figures (e.g. an alternate "20 GWh" plant referenced elsewhere is a different project).

plant_name: Hu Na Energy Sodium-ion Battery and System Project (Jiaxing)
operator: Zhejiang Hu Na Energy Co., Ltd.
research_notes: Correct entity is 浙江湖钠能源 (Zhejiang Hu Na = "Lake Sodium" Energy), not to be confused with 华钠芯能 (HuaYang/Shanxi) or HiNa/Hina Battery (中科海钠). Site is in Nanhu (South Lake) District, Jiaxing, Zhejiang, on the SW side of the Qixian Road / Zhuangbo Road intersection (Xiangjiahang area). Groundbreaking 27 Sep 2023; total investment ~11bn yuan over ~504.7 mu. Full nameplate at completion: 20 GWh/yr sodium-ion cells + modules, plus a separate 1.5 GWh/yr lithium-ion MODULE (pack) line (module-only, not cells). Cell manufacturer confirmed: makes sodium-ion cells (50Ah+ prismatic-type cells, layered-oxide cathode + hard-carbon anode, >130 Wh/kg). Two phases: Phase 1 ~154.7 mu, ~2bn yuan, 4 GWh/yr sodium cells+modules + 1.5 GWh Li-ion modules. Phase 1 main structure topped out (reported both ~Aug 2025 and Dec 2024 across sources) with ~70% of construction complete and production 'expected shortly' as of the sources — hence status under_construction rather than operational. nameplate_capacity_gwh=20 is the eventual full sodium-ion cell+module nameplate; no confirmed reference/ramp years available so capacity_ref_year and capacity_by_year_json left null. Coordinates not precisely sourced. End market spans home/industrial energy storage and low-speed vehicles (mixed). Chinese-language corroboration: bjx.com.cn (2023-09-28), itdcw.com, ofweek libattery. English: ess-news.com (2025-11-24), company site hunaen.com (unreachable via fetch).

plant_name: Shaanxi Green Energy Storage LFP Cell Plant Yulin
operator: Shaanxi Green Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd.
parent_company: Shaanxi Green Energy Co., Ltd. (Shaanxi Environmental Protection Industry Group)
research_notes: Shaanxi Green Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd. is a provincial state-owned subsidiary (established September 2025) of Shaanxi Green Energy Co., Ltd., under Shaanxi Environmental Protection Industry Group. Its production base in the Yulin Economic and Technological Development Zone (Shaanxi, NW China) rolled out the first batch of a record 3,777 Ah large-format LFP energy storage cell in early May 2026 (actual capacity >=3,900 Ah, >95% round-trip efficiency, ~12,000 cycle life), which coincided with commissioning of a 2 GWh/year smart manufacturing line built around the product - hence status "operational" and nameplate 2 GWh for 2026. Cells target grid-side standalone storage, renewable-base projects, C&I storage and mobile emergency storage (end market ESS). The very large-format cell is prismatic. Company signals intent to build a broader storage ecosystem (DC prefab cabins, mobile storage fast-charging vehicles), but no confirmed capacity-expansion figures were found - so capacity_by_year is single-year. Precise plant coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Sources: ess-news.com (English trade press, 2026-05-08) and Shaanxi Daily / sxdaily.com.cn (Chinese state media, 2026-05-09); corroborated by cn.solarbe.com (2026-05-07). Confidence 0.7: consistent single-tier reputable trade/official reporting, but capacity is a first-line figure and coordinates/expansion unconfirmed.

plant_name: Gotion Sodium Plant Tangshan
research_notes: Gotion High-tech operates existing GWh-scale sodium-ion battery cell production lines in Tangshan (Hebei, China) and Hefei, as confirmed at the 17 May 2026 launch of its "Gnascent" sodium-ion battery brand (three variants: High-Energy 261 Wh/kg; Power 162 Wh/kg down to -50C; Energy Storage 180Ah single cell, >20,000 cycles). Chemistry is sodium-ion; cells are used across both EV/power and stationary energy storage applications, hence end_market = mixed. Sources describe the Tangshan lines as already established and "GWh-scale", so status is set to operational, but no source gives a specific nameplate GWh figure for the Tangshan site alone, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null. Note: large-scale mass production of the Energy Storage variant is planned for Q4 2026 on these existing lines, so the site may be better described as ramping. No specific site coordinates, start year, or cell format confirmed. Gotion's stated total group manufacturing base is ~400 GWh across 20 bases by end-2025, but that is a global figure and does not apply to Tangshan. Confidence 0.5 due to unsourced capacity and some ambiguity between "existing operational lines" and "mass production from Q4 2026". Other corroborating sources: carnewschina.com (2026-05-17), cleantechnica.com (2026-05-22), S&P autotechinsight.spglobal.com.

plant_name: Gotion Gnascent Sodium-Ion Plant Hefei
research_notes:
Real site. Gotion High-tech (Hefei-headquartered, Volkswagen is largest shareholder) launched its "Gnascent" sodium-ion battery brand at its 15th Global Technology Conference on 17 May 2026. Existing, highly automated GWh-scale sodium-ion cell production lines are reported as operational in both Tangshan and Hefei; large-scale mass production of the energy-storage variant is planned for Q4 2026. This is genuine battery CELL manufacturing (sodium-ion), so is_cell_manufacturer=true.

Chemistry: sodium-ion. Three variants launched — High-Energy (261 Wh/kg), Power (162 Wh/kg, -50C operation, commercial vehicles/outdoor), and Energy Storage (180Ah single cell, >20,000 cycles). End market spans EV/commercial vehicles and stationary storage, hence "mixed".

Cell format: not explicitly stated in sources; recorded as "prismatic" as a plausible inference for a 180Ah large-format storage cell — treat as low-confidence/unconfirmed.

Capacity: sources only describe the Hefei sodium line as "GWh-scale" — no specific annual GWh figure for the sodium-ion line at Hefei was found, so nameplate_capacity_gwh is left null rather than guessed. (Gotion's total group energy-storage/manufacturing footprint was cited as ~400 GWh across 20 global bases by end-2025, but that is a company-wide figure, not this plant's sodium line, so it was not used.) A separately reported "20 GWh Hefei plant supplying Volkswagen" appears to relate to Gotion's LFP/unified-cell VW supply rather than the Gnascent sodium line, so it was not attributed here.

Status: the Hefei production lines are described as already operational (GWh-scale lines "confirmed operational in Tangshan and Hefei"), with Gnascent sodium mass production ramping Q4 2026 — hence status=operational and start_year=2026.

Coordinates not sourced (left null). Cross-checked across CleanTechnica, CarNewsChina, S&P Global AutoTechInsight, and battery-energy-storage-system.com; capacity specifics for the sodium line were consistently vague ("GWh-scale") across all sources.

plant_name: Taiji Sodium Cylindrical Cell Base Jingzhou
research_notes: Taiji Sodium (Jingzhou) Technology Co., Ltd. filed its sodium-ion battery production base project for approval on 17 June 2026. On full completion the site is planned to output 3 GWh/year of large-format cylindrical sodium-ion cells plus matching ESS modules; it makes cells (highly automated large-cylindrical sodium-ion cell lines) alongside PACK/module lines. Total investment RMB 1.5bn, 121 mu land, ~97,000 sqm floor area. Construction scheduled to begin September 2026, so status is announced (not yet under construction as of the source date). Located in Jingzhou, Hubei Province; exact site coordinates not disclosed, left null. Parent/operator entity founded June 2026 with RMB 50m registered capital. Capacity is the eventual full nameplate; no ramp schedule or specific full-capacity year was published, so capacity_ref_year and capacity_by_year_json left null. Single trade-press source (EnergyTrend, corroborated by SMM) — confidence moderate. End market recorded as ESS given the energy-storage module focus.

plant_name: Easton Sodium-ion Cell Plant Dongguan (Songshan Lake)

Capacity/status should be upgraded once the company annual report or IR PDF is directly accessible.

plant_name: Chuneng New Energy Xiaogan Base (Xiaogan Lithium Battery Industrial Park)
research_notes: Chuneng New Energy's Xiaogan (Hubei) Lithium Battery Industrial Park. Construction started 8 May 2022; Phase 1 (>30 GWh designed annual capacity, three cell factories / nine automated lines, plus module-pack and ESS container plants) came online 28 June 2023 — the site manufactures battery cells (电芯), so it is a genuine cell manufacturer. Full park planned at 150 GWh/yr total nameplate on 3,335+ acres, positioned as China's largest single battery production base; nameplate_capacity_gwh=150 reflects the full planned build-out, with capacity_ref_year left null as no target year for the full 150 GWh is confirmed. capacity_by_year_json records the confirmed Phase 1 ~30 GWh from 2023 (later reported ramping toward ~35 GWh as more lines came online). Chemistry LFP (磷酸铁锂); Chuneng produces large prismatic cells (e.g. its 314Ah "Chuneng No.1" ESS cell), hence prismatic format. End market mixed: both power/EV batteries and energy-storage (ESS) cells/systems. Not a JV. Precise site coordinates not sourced, left null (site is in Xiaogan, Hubei Province). Sources: Hubei Daily/cnhubei (28 Jun 2023), Xiaogan municipal government, Hubei Provincial DIIT, and battery trade press; company reports total footprint (Wuhan, Xiaogan, Yichang, Xiangyang) exceeding 110 GWh effective capacity.

plant_name: Greater Bay Technology Nansha Plant
operator: Greater Bay Technology (Guangzhou Juwan Technology Research)
chemistry: lithium-ion (XFC extreme fast-charge); solid-state in development
research_notes: World's first professional XFC (extreme fast-charging) power-battery factory, at Greater Bay Technology's Nansha HQ base, Guangzhou (Dongyong section, Nansha Avenue; ~189,000 sqm; ~RMB 4bn investment; construction launched May 2022). It is a genuine cell manufacturer: the cell (电芯) workshop began trial production in Oct 2023 and module/pack lines were formally put into production on 30 April 2024 — hence status operational, start_year 2023. Phase 1 nameplate is 4 GWh/yr (operational, ~120,000 EVs), expandable to a total planned 8 GWh/yr; full 8 GWh is the eventual nameplate but phase-2 completion date is not confirmed, so capacity_by_year_json records only the confirmed 4 GWh at 2024. Chemistry is XFC lithium-ion (fast-charge Li-ion; specific cathode not stated in sources); the company rolled out all-solid-state A-sample cells in April 2026 targeting GWh-scale mass production. Ownership: GAC-incubated (founded Sep 2020); in Dec 2024 GAC Group sold 18.82% to controlling shareholder GAC Industrial Group, retaining ~15.6% indirectly. A separate 8 GWh energy-storage (ESS) production base was also broken ground in Nansha (Feb 2023) — this row covers the XFC EV power-battery factory. No precise GPS coordinates or cell format confirmed by sources, left null. Capacity/status corroborated by Just Auto (2023-11-01), Nansha government release, EnergyTrend and GAC corporate pages.

plant_name: Jiangsu Tafel New Energy Nanjing Plant
research_notes: Cell manufacturer producing prismatic aluminium-shell lithium-ion power/ESS cells (ternary NMC and LFP). Located in Jiangning District, Nanjing (Jiangning/Airport Economic Development Zone; reported address No. 249 Lantian Road). Phase I ~1.5 GWh was operational; Phase II (3 GWh, targeted mid-2021) and Phase III (3 GWh, targeted end-2021) added under a ~3bn yuan investment, giving the Nanjing site roughly 6-7.5 GWh/yr at full build. Capacity figures conflict across sources: phased sum (1.5+3+3) implies 7.5 GWh; some Chinese sources cite ~6.5 GWh full Nanjing build. Company (founded 2014, HQ Nanjing) was materially weakened around 2020-2021 by a CATL patent-infringement suit that suspended its IPO; current operating state of the Nanjing plant in 2026 is unconfirmed - status set 'operational' on the basis of Phase I production and phase build-out, but with reduced confidence. Coordinates left null (only development-zone-level location found, ~31.1N 118.13E for Jiangning Dev Zone, not the specific site). Sources: metal.com/SMM, gev.org.cn, Chinese trade press (cbea.com, in-en.com).

plant_name: Highpower International Huizhou Plant (Longhu/Tonghu Industrial Park)
parent_company: Shenzhen Highpower Technology Co., Ltd. (豪鹏科技, SZSE: 001283)

research_notes: Highpower (founded 2001/2002, Shenzhen; US-listed Highpower International went private ~2019, Chinese entity Shenzhen Highpower Technology / 豪鹏科技 re-listed on SZSE main board 2022 under code 001283). An energy-storage battery-cell project at the park is designed for ~3 GWh/year of ESS cells (residential, C&I and data-centre storage), plus a steel-shell stacked-cell line of ~32 million cells/year; total investment ~RMB 447 million. In Jan 2026 the parent announced a share placement of up to RMB 800 million to further expand energy-storage and AI-battery capacity (official SZSE/cninfo disclosure dated 2026-01-06: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-01-06/1224918899.PDF). nameplate_capacity_gwh=3 refers ONLY to the energy-storage cell project (GWh); the far larger consumer Li-ion output is quoted in units/month and cannot be reliably converted to GWh, so total site GWh is likely higher but unsourced. Coordinates left null (Tonghu is roughly in western Huizhou but no precise site coords confirmed). Chemistry of ESS cells not explicitly confirmed as LFP. Confidence moderate: GWh figure is single-project and site is a mixed consumer+ESS operation.

plant_name: Nandu Power (Narada) Hangzhou/Fuyang Lithium Cell Base

NAME AMBIGUITY: 富阳 (Fuyang District, Hangzhou, Zhejiang = HQ base) is distinct from 阜阳 (Fuyang City, Anhui, which administers the Jieshi/Huatuo base); English sources conflate them. plant_name: Shenzhen BetterPower Shenzhen Plant (Longhua base)
